documents_expected.why: who can apply, eligible projects, maximum, rolling process
application form: sections, budget table, landowner and Tribe letters
programme summary: eligible locations and prioritisation criteria

eligibility.rule: Community-based organisations in economically disadvantaged communities (EDCs)
eligibility.quote: Community-based organizations in EDCs are eligible to apply for Community Grants.

eligibility.rule: Habitat project on the San Francisco Bay shoreline (flood or access work only as part of one)
eligibility.quote: A habitat project that aims to restore, protect, or enhance tidal wetlands, managed ponds, or natural habitats on the shoreline in the San Francisco Bay Area;
The maximum amount that the Authority will provide for a Community Grant is $300,000.

eligibility.rule: Applicant's capacity and history count toward likelihood of success
eligibility.quote: Applicant's capacity and resources to complete and maintain the project • Applicant history

documents.item: Application form (4–5 pages): description, schedule, preliminary budget, history, partners, community support
documents.quote: The application should not be longer than 4-5 pages (not counting maps or photos).

documents.item: Landowner's letter agreeing to host the project, if not the landowner
documents.quote: if you are not the landowner, a letter from the landowner confirming their willingness to host the project will be required.

documents.item: Letter from Tribal leadership, if a Tribe is involved
documents.quote: If a Tribe, please provide a letter from their leadership confirming their involvement with your final application

documents.item: Optional maps, designs and photos, with a rights confirmation
documents.quote: You may attach location maps, designs, plans, engineering drawings, color photographs, etc., to help describe your proposal.

effort.quote: You can apply at any time. We are accepting and reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

effort.step: Consultation with staff, then a revised application for final review
effort.quote: Staff will schedule a consultation with you to talk through the project, and a review team will assess whether the project is a good fit for the Community Grants Program.

effort.step: Board approval, then about two months to a grant agreement
effort.quote: It usually takes about two months from the time the board approves the project to getting a grant agreement in place

notes: An easier path than the Authority's competitive round, with a shorter form and staff help. Shoreline means the nine Bay Area counties, excluding the Delta primary zone. Partnering with a restoration agency or landowner is common but not required. No reporting duties are stated on these pages.
